summary: Implement concurrent pool storage and master-owned VM admission. API impact: changed/new contracts, including BUG-0141 readiness report negotiation through existing capability fields; BUG-0146 retains existing setup/status/reconciliation contracts without a schema change; BUG-0147 uses the existing status GET contract without a schema change. BUG-0146's Core rollout and idle observation passed; BUG-0147's UI publication and native outage/recovery workflow passed. The latest preparation passed its prerequisite gates, but the six-writer 600 MiB attempt stopped before its intended fault when counter serialization failed; target DataOut/fencing investigation and native acceptance remain in progress; the reviewed disposable IBLOCK fixture passed copy/restore and no-VM cold checks, and a later bounded full writer/fault/return run passed after target-only fencing and verified survivor files; fresh NFS/SMB repeats and GFS lock probes passed; fresh Controller B re-adoption passed a bounded Core-owned inventory/native-identity acceptance without a schema or new state record.

guide.reason: Shared cluster setup, admission and failure states need operator instructions; current implementation and walkthrough gates remain open. BUG-0140 changes archive ownership metadata only, with no operator workflow or API impact; contents and notices remain unchanged. BUG-0142 corrects disposable verification cleanup only: guide/API impact none because product behavior and contracts are unchanged, and no durable pool state is added. BUG-0144 updates stop-only recovery instructions and frozen-I/O limitations; its narrow healthy-storage/master-service-unavailable check passed, while lost-quorum/frozen-I/O completion remains open. BUG-0145 changes disposable domain XML only: guide/API impact none and no new product state; controlled cold boot passed but write-time resilience remains open. BUG-0146 is internal quiet idempotence during member reconciliation, with no operator workflow change. BUG-0147 updates storage guidance because unavailable/checking status is distinct from confirmed empty configuration; its UI publication and native outage/recovery workflow passed. The stable storage-row attribute is UI-only, with no API, durable-state or operator-workflow change.

api.reason: Typed shared-block profiles, transient setup/status relay and authenticated Core peer operations change the public and host contracts. BUG-0125/0127 tighten native fencing configuration and monitor readiness; BUG-0128 adds native DLM compatibility prerequisites through the existing setup/status contract. BUG-0130 separates initial activation from strict-majority runtime readiness and adds an observed degraded status. BUG-0131/0132 add exact internal peer update reservation, authenticated prior-definition comparison, journal-backed commit/abort and durable acknowledgements, with Core-side outcome confirmation through existing operator APIs. BUG-0133 restricts runtime reconciliation to fresh owner evidence. BUG-0134/0135 use existing setup/status and admission contracts for native external-request off mapping and retention of the private activation receipt across exact retries. BUG-0137 requires exact current proof acknowledgement through existing Status.Fences before reports count as healthy and immediately persists degradation after exclusion. BUG-0138 adds optional session_monitor_ready to observed cluster status and an internal monitor-only CLI contract: readiness proves the installed adapter and a successful exact live session probe, not aggregate cluster health. Older members omit readiness and block transport activation. BUG-0146 changes no schema: it uses the existing setup, status and reconciliation contract to make exact healthy member state read-only. BUG-0147 changes no schema: the existing storage status GET distinguishes unavailable/checking from confirmed-empty state. BUG-0146's native rollout established its idle no-op behavior; BUG-0147's existing status workflow passed without a schema change, while broader native acceptance remains open. No Controller-owned state is introduced.

roadmap.reason: Implementation is not accepted yet; the published roadmap must not claim completed shared-block storage or HA.

state.reason: The pool master owns desired cluster configuration, operation progress and VM execution assignment; Controller only relays requests and observations. BUG-0146 reuses this existing Core state. BUG-0147 adds no durable state.
state.record: Core pool-storage-cluster.json and pool-vms.json complement the existing managed storage journal; root-only credentials are separate. VM pending_update records retain the prior master definition and exact next operation/revision until matching journal evidence commits or proves an unapplied failure; one bounded last_aborted_update receipt allows exact lost-ack replay until the next reservation. Retained successful VM/storage journals preserve historical shared ownership after disk removal or detach; no separate member policy store is added. First local-to-shared updates seed only from the ready authenticated owner's exact current-generation prior inventory, and runtime reconciliation uses only fresh owner observations. The cluster operation's private initial-activation receipt binds complete setup evidence to the exact request, configuration and membership; it is not inferred from historical status. Local pool-vm-autostart-attempts markers bind runtime attempts to the actual OS boot without adding a policy or Controller dependency. BUG-0146 adds no record: it reads the existing owned configuration and unit state before using the current recovery path. BUG-0147 adds no record: the browser projects Core's existing status response. Fresh Controller access reads setup/status from the master and adopts the existing storage/VM inventory; internal activation receipts and local attempt markers need no Controller reconstruction. Peer replicas are generation-bound. Bounded fresh-Controller re-adoption passed; strict continuous-writer handover and untested outage paths remain open acceptance gates.

verification.method: Focused regressions and independent safety review accompany native six-VM workloads separately on one iSCSI LUN, one NFS export and one SMB share. Backend writes, reboot hashes, locking, explicit fence/return and autostart passed on their documented builds. After BUG-0138, two corrected stopped-VM transport repeats fenced only the isolated host and preserved both survivors; live-write transport acceptance remains open. BUG-0139 presentation/action gating uses existing host freshness without new durable state; the reviewed UI/source publication and a native all-stale outage/recovery workflow passed with management restored and full native postflight. BUG-0141 negotiated reports passed source tests and older-Controller native status recovery; complete management-outage acceptance remains open. BUG-0142 cleanup regressions passed independent review, 41 shared workload tests and 18 private outage tests. BUG-0143 is unresolved: actual target DataOut session closures caused native exclusion before intended fault injection; subsequent quorum recovery also failed. Preparation passed six boots, baseline writes and headroom, but the following six-writer 600 MiB attempt crashed serializing tuple-keyed counters after two growth samples and before its intended fault. Target DataOut failures then affected two Cores; one was fenced, the other recovered, and containment confirmed every guest off. The corrected helper has source regression review but has not rerun the scenario. A reviewed offline copy retained the original FILEIO backing; canonical IBLOCK restore passed semantic target-configuration comparison after an invalid first LUN reference. Storage-target reboot and three-Core zero-guest cold-return checks passed, as did a target-only no-VM interruption and explicit return. After a passed post-archive preflight, a full IBLOCK attempt completed six boots, baselines, two growth samples per writer and its intended fault. Only the selected Core fenced without observed DataOut, but the immediate history sample reported the expected in-flight fence as `pending` without a completed event and still showed three-member membership, so the run failed. Four completed 600 MiB survivor files passed expected-hash and second-reread checks, not a full writer transcript. Explicit recovery restored all three Cores with zero guests; all six guests are now off. A corrected bounded convergence poll then supported a second full IBLOCK run: six writers passed two growth samples, the intended dual-target interruption fenced only its selected Core without observed DataOut, four 600 MiB survivor files passed expected-hash/second-reread checks across the fault/fence window, and two polls saw completed fencing then ready survivors. Controlled return observed a new target boot identity, unchanged baseline hashes and canonical storage identity; fresh API stop/native zero-guest checks passed. This is bounded disposable-IBLOCK scenario evidence only, not production HA, migration, physical SAN, soak, replacement or current-ISO acceptance. Fresh NFS and SMB repeats passed overlapping six-VM 32 MiB fsync writes, all-guest reboot/hash checks and real non-root cross-host lock refusal followed by a 512-byte post-release write; both reached native zero-guest checks. The latest GFS lock probe passed the equivalent lock/refusal/release check. Fresh Controller B re-adopted all three Cores from Core-local records with unchanged membership, peer trust, storage/native configuration and pool identities; six guest boot identities and 600 MiB rereads matched. Its applied inventory matched 18 VMs and three repositories; four failed outcomes remain operations with no native failed VM. This is not full historic route equivalence because earlier collections include failed/empty input outcomes. The strict continuous-writer A-to-B experiment failed from private fixture connectivity issues, though original writers completed before adoption. Final B reconciliation observed six freshly off guests and all-three native zero state; B is active, A data retained and rollback did not run. A cold no-VM interruption fenced only its target and an explicit return restored native health on all three Cores with no workload guests; that cold test establishes no guest-write/hash result. BUG-0144 source/API/guide review and focused/full/race checks passed; a narrow native force-stop with master management unavailable but healthy quorum/storage observed the VM off without changing its owner journal or minting a permit. Lost-quorum/frozen-I/O completion remains open. BUG-0145 isolated the ACPI/headless-VGA reset interaction and added internal VGA without a graphics endpoint. Exact cold boots now expose two CPUs on all four hosts; the same target configuration/identities and healthy three-member reports were verified. The checkpoint passed full Go, 215 Python tests and independent source/archive parity; final fixture regressions passed. BUG-0146's regression, focused/race/full vmhost checks, independent review, Core rollout and post-fix no-VM idle observation passed. The pre-fix window saw 60 reload requests and 60 `Reloading` lines per member; the post-fix window saw none while Corosync inode/timestamp remained stable. This does not establish DataOut causality. BUG-0147 source UI checks, fixture coverage, independent visual review, UI publication and its native outage/recovery workflow passed. Three isolated development ISOs were built and independently audited; the third includes the final fixture correction and its eight promoted distribution entries replaced the prior recoverable set, but it predates BUG-0146. Broader interruptions, strict continuous-writer handover, untested outage paths and native final acceptance remain open; these results do not establish production HA.
